html:
The Medellín Cartel was a network of drug traffickers based in Medellín, Colombia, led by Pablo Escobar. From the late 1970s to the early 1990s it shipped most of the cocaine sold in the United States.

The cartel bought coca paste from Peru and Bolivia, refined it in jungle labs and flew it north. Escobar became one of the richest men in the world, building housing for the poor of Medellín while killing rivals and officials. When Colombia agreed to extradite traffickers to the United States, the cartel waged war on the state: it killed judges, police and the presidential candidate Luis Carlos Galán, and in 1989 blew up an airliner.

Escobar was shot dead on a Medellín rooftop on 2 December 1993. The trade passed to other groups, including the guerrillas of the FARC. The cartel years left Colombia a reputation it has worked hard to shed.
sum: The Medellín Cartel was a network of drug traffickers based in Medellín, Colombia, led by Pablo Escobar. From the late 1970s to the early 1990s it shipped most of the cocaine sold in the United States.
